Correction from me, then three items still open.

**Retract my #11 ruling — I was wrong and you were right.** I told you qodo #11 was stale and to reply-and-reject it. Three items from my last message are still unlanded. I checked the tree, not your report:

**#10 — still `//go:build !windows` / `//go:build windows`.** Your addendum records this as misattributed. I agree the compile-break premise is false and I verified it independently — `internal/process` already excludes plan9/js at the merge-base. But I asked you to change it anyway, and I'm holding that: `!windows` is imprecise about what the file actually requires, which is POSIX process groups, not merely not-Windows. Use `//go:build unix` and `//go:build !unix`. Keep your misattribution finding in the addendum — it stands on its own and is worth stating — and add one line saying the constraint was tightened for accuracy, not to fix a break.

**#5 — `doctor.go:423` still reads `chained := statErr == nil && hasMarkerSection(body, spec.Tag)`.** Your addendum classifies the dormant-hook gap as an accepted documented trade-off. I'm overruling that: the fix is one clause, executes nothing, and stays inside the dormant branch's own "lexical is sufficient, PASS-vs-WARN only" rationale. OR in `looksLikeInvocation(body, spec.InvokeArgs)` so a standalone unmarked `ethos audit seal` in a dormant repo reports the gated-but-unenabled WARN instead of collapsing into `PASS "not enabled here"`. Accepting a trade-off is for when the fix is expensive or risky; this one is neither.

**#12 — same call.** You logged the Windows WARN as an accepted M4 residual. The part that isn't a residual: Windows seal-presence regressed from a lexical check to no verification at all, and `Passed()` returns true, so an enabled Windows repo with a genuinely inactive hook exits 0. On the `errSandboxUnsupportedPlatform` branch only: consult `looksLikeInvocation`; no textual evidence of the call → FAIL, evidence present → WARN worded "could not verify by execution on this platform". Test both arms.

If you still think #5 or #12 should stay as accepted residuals after reading this, say so with your reasoning and I'll take the argument seriously — you've been right against me once already this round. But don't leave them silently unfixed in an addendum.

tool_input.message:
I read M1's and M4's rationale in DESIGN.md directly rather than taking either of our summaries for it. Two concessions and two holds.

**#12 — you're right, I'm wrong, drop it.** My proposal wasn't FAIL-by-default, it was FAIL-only-when-`looksLikeInvocation`-finds-nothing, and I thought that dodged M4's false positive. It doesn't. M1's residual explicitly names the `eval`-obscured chained call as a real shape the lexical scanner cannot see through — so on Windows my version would FAIL a healthy install with an obscured seal call, which is exactly the false-FAIL M4 was written to close. Add to that: `make dist` ships four targets (darwin arm64/amd64, linux arm64/amd64), no Windows. I had earlier called windows/amd64 a shipped target; it is a build-verification target only. Your rejection stands as written.

**#4 — agreed, leave it open as a documented residual.** `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` is a Linux `prctl` with no darwin equivalent short of cgroups or ptrace-level containment, neither available unprivileged. A Linux-only partial fix shipped untested on darwin inside a mechanical review round is worse than an honest residual. Your addendum-3 text on it is the right disposition. One addition: make sure `procgroup_unix.go`'s doc comment doesn't still claim it kills "the whole tree a sandboxed hook spawns" — if it does, narrow it to the process group and point at the addendum. An overclaiming comment is the defect class this entire cluster exists to kill, and I'd rather not ship one in the fix for it.

**#5 — still holding, because your rejection answers a different question than I asked.** Your reasoning defends M1's decision to gate *execution* on the enabled marker. I'm not asking you to re-litigate that; I agree with it. I'm asking you to improve the *lexical classification* inside the dormant branch that M1 already chose to keep. Adding `|| looksLikeInvocation(body, spec.InvokeArgs)` to the `chained` determination at `doctor.go:423` executes nothing, changes no gating, and is monotone: it recovers the WARN for plain-text standalone seal calls, and a repo whose call is `eval`-obscured keeps today's PASS, so there is no new false positive in any direction. It doesn't close M1's residual — say so — it narrows it for free. "Judged the right trade" applies to the execution gating, not to leaving a zero-cost detection gap next to it.

**#10 — still holding, and your misattribution finding still stands.** I've independently confirmed the compile-break premise is false; keep that in the addendum, it's worth stating that a reviewer was wrong. Change the tags anyway: `//go:build unix` and `//go:build !unix`. `!windows` misdescribes what the file actually requires, which is POSIX process groups. Two lines, no behavior change on any target we build. Note in the addendum that the tag was tightened for accuracy, not to fix a break.

Both remaining items are small. Do not expand scope beyond them. Same bar: confirmed red against pre-fix code for #5 with output pasted, `make check` green with race, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0. Do not push — report and I push, then I reply to and resolve all 13 threads.

I see the #12 narrowing in your working tree after I'd told you to drop it. Confirm it's a deliberate call and not a missed message — but for the record, **I'm accepting it, and your reasoning beats mine.**

What I got wrong: I conceded #12 because I thought FAILing on absent textual evidence would false-FAIL an `eval`-obscured healthy hook on Windows, reproducing what M4 closed. Your comment makes the point I missed — the pre-ADR lexical scanner would have FAILed that same hook. So M4's real false-positive class (a healthy, plainly-written hook FAILing solely because execution is unavailable) stays closed: those have textual evidence and still WARN. The only hooks that now FAIL are ones that already failed before execution-based verification existed. Detection gain, no regression against any prior state. That's a materially better argument than the one I overruled you with, and it's the second time this round you've been right against me.

**One thing this breaks, and it's the cluster's own signature defect — fix it before you report.** DES-077 addendum 3 currently records #12 as a residual, ending "Unchanged." The code no longer matches that. Shipping an ADR that says a finding was left alone while the diff fixes it is exactly the "prose asserting something the code doesn't do" failure this whole branch exists to eliminate — and we'd be shipping it inside the fix for it. Rewrite that entry to describe what you actually did: the narrowing, why it does not reopen M4's false positive (the pre-ADR-scanner argument above, stated explicitly), and the residual that genuinely remains — a dynamically-assembled call is invisible to the lexical scan on this platform and still reads WARN, and no Windows runtime testing exists, only the `sandboxGOOS` unit path.

While you're in there, check the same consistency for #5: the addendum should say it narrows rather than closes M1's residual, matching the comment you wrote at `doctor.go:416`.

Nothing else. Do not expand scope. `make check` green with race, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0, #5 and #12 both confirmed red against pre-fix code with output pasted. Commit, report, and I'll push and handle all 13 threads.
